body_markdown:
With SEMA well and truly underway in Las Vegas, titans of the aftermarket industry are rolling out their heavy hitters. These astonishing builds show off these companies’ parts, capabilities, and vision. Yesterday we were introduced to two neat vehicles from Ford Performance: a[Mustang celebrating 125 years of Ford Racing](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/celebrate-125-years-with-the-ford-racing-r125-mustang/) and a modest but lovely[’85 Ford F-250](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/this-1985-bullnose-f-250-isnt-semas-flashiest-build-but-it-might-be-our-favorite/) built by an Oregon mechanical engineer. The Fat Fender Garage GT/FX is decidedly more extreme.


Who couldn’t fall in love with an 800-hp, 1956 Ford F-100 that juices classic Ford truck styling with startling modern performance? It is, by any measure, an absolutely nutty street truck. Let’s dig in.


Fat Fender Garage


Fat Fender Garage


Fat Fender Garage


Based in Gilbert, Arizona,[Fat Fender Garage](https://fatfender.com/) specializes in aftermarket support for classic Ford and Chevrolet pickups, offering everything from off-the-shelf engine upgrades to custom-built chassis swaps. The GT/FX is meant to showcase the breadth and depth of Fat Fender’s full arsenal. The company says that there are more than 15,000 hours of design, engineering, and fabrication into this build. Yeesh.


Fat Fender Garage


The real showstopper, of course, is under the hood: That’s a third-gen Ford 5.0-liter Coyote V-8 topped with a massive 3.0-liter[Whipple supercharger](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-squeezes-supercharged-v-8-power-mr-whipple-likely-furious/) . Power figures are appropriately silly: Fat Fender says this mill produces 800 hp and 750 lb-ft of torque. It pairs with a Ford 10R80 10-speed automatic transmission to drive the rear wheels. A bespoke three-inch exhaust with Borla XR-1 Raceline mufflers, JMD Resonators, and electric cutouts to really let this motor shout when you want it to.


Fat Fender Garage


That powertrain mounts to a custom FF1 Performance Coilover chassis that the company says sharpens body control, stability, and cornering behavior. The steel body was fabricated entirely by hand, allowing for numerous tweaks to give this truck an even more menacing curbside presence. The hood and roof were both flattened, while the cab was sectioned by two inches. Front and rear fenders were widened to swallow those custom 20-inch HRE wheels. The only remaining piece of bodywork from the Ford factory is the grille.


Fat Fender Garage


Fat Fender Garage


Inside, there’s a fully bespoke interior from Fat Fender with custom upholstered leather seats and a leather dashpad. A concealed HVAC system with a single one-piece custom vent ensures at least a modicum of creature comfort. Likewise, a set of modern gauges and an upgraded audio system almost make you think this thing could be a pleasant place to spend hours on end.


Fat Fender Garage


Fat Fender says this truck combines “classic F-Series styling with the presence and performance of the modern-era Ford GT.” Not so sure about that; to us, the second ingredient is more like the recently released[Mustang Dark Horse SC](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2026-mustang-dark-horse-sc-first-drive-power-chord/) . Still a pretty pony to hitch to one’s wagon.
